subject: Civil Engineering
title: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake
description: One-minute skill: The 1906 San Francisco Earthquake.

hook.text: At 5:12 AM on April 18, 1906, San Francisco shook for 45 seconds — and then burned for three days.

buildup.text: A magnitude 7.9 rupture along the San Andreas Fault displaced the ground 20 feet.

discovery.text: The earthquake broke water mains — firefighters couldn't stop the fires that followed.

twist.text: Over 80% of the destruction came from fire, not shaking — broken utilities were the real killer.

climax.text: 3,000 people died and 250,000 were homeless. It reshaped earthquake engineering forever.

punchline.text: The earthquake shook. The fire consumed. The lesson was: protect the lifelines.

quiz.question: Why was fire, not shaking, the primary cause of destruction in the 1906 San Francisco earthquake?
options: The earthquake was too weak to cause structural damage
Broken water mains prevented firefighters from controlling fires that spread after the quake
Gas lighting in buildings caused immediate explosions

details.summary: The 1906 San Francisco earthquake, estimated at magnitude 7.9, ruptured 477 kilometers of the San Andreas Fault and destroyed much of the city primarily through fires that burned for three days after water mains broke.
details.whyItMatters: The 1906 earthquake launched the modern science of seismology and led to Harry Fielding Reid's elastic rebound theory, which remains the fundamental explanation of how earthquakes occur.
takeaways: Fire caused 80% of the destruction after broken water mains prevented firefighting
The elastic rebound theory of earthquake mechanics was developed from this event
The disaster led to fundamental advances in seismology and building practices

faq.question: Why did fire cause more damage than the earthquake shaking itself?
faq.answer: The earthquake broke water mains throughout the city, leaving firefighters without water. Gas lines ruptured and ignited. Multiple fires merged into massive conflagrations that burned for three days. The fire department resorted to dynamiting buildings to create firebreaks.

faq.question: What lasting impact did the 1906 earthquake have on earthquake science?
faq.answer: Harry Fielding Reid studied the fault displacement and developed elastic rebound theory, explaining that earthquakes release strain energy accumulated over time. This foundational theory still underpins seismology.
